punchline: Double one grain of rice across a chessboard's 64 squares and you pass 18 quintillion, which is the shape of computing power since 1958.
thirty_sec: An old tale: one grain of rice on the first chessboard square, doubling each time. By square 32 it is about 4 billion grains; by square 64, a pile taller than Everest. Brynjolfsson and McAfee say computing has been doubling since 1958 and is in the second half of the board. In 2004 no driverless car finished a 150-mile desert race, and the best got 7.4 miles. Under six years later, Google's car had logged hundreds of thousands of miles.
